title: Discovery of the Immaculate Constellation briefing on a Pentagon classified system
place_text: Pentagon, OSD Under Secretary of Defense for Policy office

tellings.quote: Uh so immaculate constellation uh it's a or it was described to me at least in my limited exposure as a operational SAP governing the intelligence surveillance and reconnaissance of UAP um around the world using tasked and unts.

plain: A former Defense Department official named Matthew Brown says that while working in a Pentagon policy office around 2018 he came across a classified briefing on a program called Immaculate Constellation, described to him as an operational secret program for watching and tracking UFOs "around the world" with military sensors, some pointed at them on purpose and some catching them by chance. He tells Michels this firsthand in 2026. The unsigned report on the program that went to Congress in 2024 says its author got the material "while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense" and calls it "a global surveillance and reconnaissance mission"; Brown later said he wrote that report as a summary of the briefing, so the report and his account are one source told twice.

discussion.by: Immaculate Constellation report (anonymous, entered into the House Oversight hearing record, 13 November 2024)
discussion.text: An unsigned report that Michael Shellenberger delivered to Congress and Rep. Nancy Mace entered into the record of the House Oversight hearing of 13 November 2024 as a document from the Pentagon; it calls itself the public version of a Defense Department employee's report, cleared for release by the State Department; Matthew Brown, a former Defense Department official, later said he wrote it; and a Defense Department spokesperson said the department has no record of a program by that name. The report says its author "obtained access to this information while pursuing their lawful duties as an employee of the Department of Defense" and gives the program's mission as "collecting imagery intelligence on Unidentified Aerial Phenomena (UAP) and ARV/RV (Reproduction Vehicles) utilizing tasked and untasked U.S. military-intelligence resources", in "a global surveillance and reconnaissance mission". Matthew Brown tells of the briefing he found, which is not public, and later said he wrote the report as a summary of it, so the report and his account are one source told twice.
